assistant: El término "few-shot" en machine learning se refiere a la capacidad de un modelo para aprender de forma efectiva con una cantidad limitada de datos de entrenamiento. En otras palabras, es la capacidad de un modelo para aprender de nuevos ejemplos con poca supervisión.

En el aprendizaje supervisado tradicional, se necesitan grandes cantidades de datos de entrenamiento para entrenar un modelo con precisión. Sin embargo, en algunos casos, no es posible recopilar grandes cantidades de datos de entrenamiento o es costoso hacerlo. El aprendizaje few-shot aborda este problema al permitir que un modelo aprenda de manera efectiva con un número limitado de ejemplos.

Por ejemplo, supongamos que queremos entrenar un modelo para reconocer diferentes tipos de flores, pero solo tenemos unas pocas imágenes de cada tipo de flor. En este caso, el aprendizaje few-shot puede ser útil para entrenar un modelo preciso con solo unas pocas imágenes de cada tipo de flor.

El aprendizaje few-shot se ha convertido en un área de investigación activa en el campo del machine learning y ha dado lugar a una serie de técnicas y modelos innovadores. Algunos de los enfoques comunes en el aprendizaje few-shot incluyen el aprendizaje por similitud, el aprendizaje por transferencia y el aprendizaje meta.

user: Además de la cantidad de datos de entrenamiento, ¿qué diferencias técnicas hay entre el aprendizaje supervisado tradicional y el aprendizaje few-shot? ¿Cuál es más efectivo?

assistant: Además de la cantidad de datos de entrenamiento, hay algunas diferencias técnicas clave entre el aprendizaje supervisado tradicional y el aprendizaje few-shot:

1. En el aprendizaje supervisado tradicional, se requiere un conjunto completo de datos etiquetados para cada tarea, mientras que en el aprendizaje few-shot, solo se necesitan unos pocos ejemplos de datos etiquetados para cada tarea.
2. El aprendizaje supervisado tradicional utiliza una arquitectura de red neuronal específica para cada tarea, mientras que el aprendizaje few-shot utiliza una arquitectura de red única que se entrena en múltiples tareas.
3. En el aprendizaje supervisado tradicional, el proceso de entrenamiento puede tardar mucho tiempo y requiere muchos recursos computacionales. En el aprendizaje few-shot, el proceso de entrenamiento es mucho más rápido y requiere menos recursos computacionales.

En cuanto a cuál es más efectivo, depende de la tarea específica y de la cantidad de datos etiquetados disponibles. Si hay suficientes datos etiquetados disponibles para una tarea, es probable que el aprendizaje supervisado tradicional sea más efectivo. Si solo hay unos pocos datos etiquetados disponibles, el aprendizaje few-shot puede ser más efectivo. -- Read the Brainfuck program from the command line
local program = arg[1]

-- The Brainfuck memory
local memory = {}

    memory[i] = 0
end

-- The pointer to the current memory cell
local pointer = 1

-- The Brainfuck program counter
local pc = 1

-- Loop stack for tracking '[' and ']'
local loopStack = {}

-- Loop through the Brainfuck program
while pc <= #program do
    local c = program:sub(pc, pc)

    if c == '>' then
        pointer = pointer + 1
    elseif c == '<' then
        pointer = pointer - 1
    elseif c == '+' then
        memory[pointer] = memory[pointer] + 1
    elseif c == '-' then
        memory[pointer] = memory[pointer] - 1
    elseif c == '.' then
        io.write(string.char(memory[pointer]))
    elseif c == ',' then
        memory[pointer] = io.read(1):byte()
    elseif c == '[' then
        if memory[pointer] == 0 then
            local loopCounter = 1
            while loopCounter > 0 do
                pc = pc + 1
                local nextChar = program:sub(pc, pc)
                if nextChar == '[' then
                    loopCounter = loopCounter + 1
                elseif nextChar == ']' then
                    loopCounter = loopCounter - 1
                end
                if pc > #program then
                    error("Unmatched '['")
                end
            end
        else
            table.insert(loopStack, pc)
        end
    elseif c == ']' then
        if #loopStack == 0 then
            error("Unmatched ']'")
        else
            if memory[pointer] ~= 0 then
                pc = loopStack[#loopStack]
            else
                table.remove(loopStack, #loopStack)
            end
        end
    end

    pc = pc + 1
end

-- Check for unmatched '['
if #loopStack > 0 then
    error("Unmatched '['")
end

assistant: Ein moderner Reisepass enthält mehrere Sicherheitsmerkmale, die dazu beitragen, die Identität des Passinhabers zu überprüfen und Fälschungen zu verhindern. Einige der wichtigsten Sicherheitsmerkmale sind:

Biometrische Daten: Moderne Reisepässe enthalten biometrische Daten wie ein digitales Foto des Passinhabers und einen Fingerabdruck. Diese Daten können verwendet werden, um die Identität des Passinhabers zu überprüfen.

Mikroschrift: Reisepässe enthalten oft Mikroschrift, die mit bloßem Auge schwer zu lesen ist. Diese Mikroschrift kann jedoch mit speziellen Vergrößerungswerkzeugen gelesen werden und hilft bei der Erkennung von Fälschungen.

Wasserzeichen: Reisepässe enthalten oft ein Wasserzeichen, das bei Lichteinfall sichtbar wird. Das Wasserzeichen enthält oft das Bild des Passinhabers und hilft bei der Verhinderung von Fälschungen.

Hologramme: Reisepässe können auch Hologramme enthalten, die schwer zu fälschen sind. Diese Hologramme können ein Bild des Passinhabers, die Nationalflagge oder andere Symbole enthalten.

Sicherheitsfaden: Einige Reisepässe enthalten einen Sicherheitsfaden, der in das Passdokument eingebettet ist. Der Sicherheitsfaden kann fluoreszierend sein und/oder ein Bild oder eine Nummer enthalten, die nur unter bestimmten Bedingungen sichtbar sind.

Maschinenlesbarer Bereich: Der maschinenlesbare Bereich (MRZ) enthält maschinenlesbare Zeichen, die für die automatische Verarbeitung von Passdaten verwendet werden können. Die MRZ enthält oft die persönlichen Daten des Passinhabers sowie einen maschinenlesbaren Code.

RFID-Chip: Einige moderne Reisepässe verfügen über einen RFID-Chip, der drahtlos ausgelesen werden kann. Der Chip enthält biometrische Daten und den maschinenlesbaren Code des Passinhabers.

assistant: Un patrón de diseño es una solución reutilizable para un problema que ocurre dentro de un contexto de programación dado.

Algunos de los patrones de diseño más importantes son los siguientes:

Factory method
Una fábrica normal produce bienes; una fábrica de software produce objetos. Y no solo eso, lo hace sin especificar la clase exacta del objeto que se creará. Para lograr esto, los objetos se crean llamando a un método de fábrica en lugar de llamar a un constructor.

Singleton
El patrón singleton se utiliza para limitar la creación de una clase a un solo objeto. Esto es beneficioso cuando se necesita un objeto (y solo uno) para coordinar acciones en todo el sistema. Hay varios ejemplos en dónde debería existir una única instancia de una clase, incluidos cachés, grupos de subprocesos y registros.

Observer
Este patrón es una dependencia de uno a muchos entre objetos, de modo que cuando un objeto cambia de estado, se notifica a todos sus dependientes. Normalmente, esto se hace llamando a uno de sus métodos.
En aras de la simplicidad, piense en lo que sucede cuando sigue a alguien en Twitter. Básicamente, le estás pidiendo a Twitter que te envíe (el observador) actualizaciones de tweets de la persona (el sujeto) que seguiste. El patrón consta de dos actores, el observador que está interesado en las actualizaciones y el sujeto que genera las actualizaciones.

Strategy
El patrón de estrategia permite agrupar algoritmos relacionados bajo una abstracción, lo que permite cambiar un algoritmo o política por otro sin modificar el cliente. En lugar de implementar directamente un solo algoritmo, el código recibe instrucciones en tiempo de ejecución que especifican cuál del grupo de algoritmos ejecutar.

Adapter
Esto permite que las clases incompatibles trabajen juntas al convertir la interfaz de una clase en otra. Piense en ello como una especie de traductor: cuando dos jefes de estado que no hablan un idioma común se encuentran, generalmente un intérprete se sienta entre los dos y traduce la conversación, lo que permite la comunicación.
Si tienes dos aplicaciones, una de las cuales arroja la salida como XML y la otra requiere una entrada JSON, entonces necesitará un adaptador entre las dos para que funcionen sin problemas.

Builder
Como su nombre lo indica, se utiliza un patrón de construcción para construir objetos. A veces, los objetos que creamos pueden ser complejos, estar formados por varios subobjetos o requerir un elaborado proceso de construcción. El ejercicio de crear tipos complejos se puede simplificar utilizando el patrón de construcción. Un objeto compuesto o agregado es lo que generalmente construye un constructor.
Consideración clave: el patrón Builder puede parecer similar al patrón de "fábrica abstracta", pero una diferencia es que el patrón Builder crea un objeto paso a paso, mientras que el patrón de fábrica abstracto devuelve el objeto de una vez.

State
El patrón State encapsula los diversos estados en los que puede estar una máquina y permite que un objeto altere su comportamiento cuando cambia su estado interno. La máquina o el contexto, como se le llama en lenguaje de patrones, puede tener acciones que lo impulsen a diferentes estados. Sin el uso del patrón, el código se vuelve inflexible y está plagado de condicionales if-else.<#sep#>user: ¿Cómo y por qué se usan los diarios?

assistant: To instantiate a scene in Godot 3.5 game engine, you can follow these steps:

1. Create the scene you want to instantiate as a separate .tscn file.
2. In the scene where you want to instantiate the other scene, add a Node2D or other node that will serve as the parent for the instantiated scene.
3. Select the parent node and click the "Add Child Node" button in the bottom right corner of the screen.
4. In the "Create Node" dialog, select "Load" and navigate to the .tscn file of the scene you want to instantiate.
5. Select the .tscn file and click "Load."
6. The instantiated scene will now appear in the scene tree as a child of the parent node you selected.

You can now customize the instantiated scene as needed. You can also use scripting to dynamically instantiate scenes at runtime using the <code>load</code> and <code>instance</code> methods. For example:

    # Load the scene as a PackedScene
    var scene = load("res://scenes/MyScene.tscn")
    
    # Instance the scene as a Node
    var instance = scene.instance()
    
    # Add the instance as a child of the current node
    add_child(instance)

Note that you'll need to replace "res://scenes/MyScene.tscn" with the path to your own scene file.

user: I'm currently making a 2d platform, how would I go about making a menu that contains an inventory, and a list of how many enemies destroyed and how many lives are left.

assistant: To create a menu with an inventory, enemy count, and lives count in a 2D platformer using Godot, follow these steps:

1. Create a new scene for the menu:
   - Click on "Scene" > "New Scene" in the top-left corner.
   - Add a "CanvasLayer" node as the root node. This will ensure that the menu is drawn on top of the game scene.
   - Save the scene as "Menu.tscn" or another name of your choice.

2. Design the menu layout:
   - Add a "Control" node as a child of the "CanvasLayer" node. This will serve as a container for the menu elements.
   - Add a "VBoxContainer" node as a child of the "Control" node. This will automatically arrange the menu elements vertically.
   - Add "Label" nodes as children of the "VBoxContainer" node for each menu element (inventory, enemy count, and lives count). Name them accordingly (e.g., "InventoryLabel", "EnemyCountLabel", "LivesCountLabel").

3. Create a script for the menu:
   - Select the "Control" node and click the "Attach Script" button in the top-right corner.
   - Choose a name and location for the script (e.g., "Menu.gd") and click "Create".
   - In the script, create variables to store the references to the "Label" nodes:

```gdscript
onready var inventory_label = $VBoxContainer/InventoryLabel
onready var enemy_count_label = $VBoxContainer/EnemyCountLabel
onready var lives_count_label = $VBoxContainer/LivesCountLabel
```

4. Update the menu with game data:
   - In the script, create a function to update the menu with the current inventory, enemy count, and lives count. You can pass these values as arguments to the function:

```gdscript
func update_menu(inventory: Array, enemy_count: int, lives_count: int):
    inventory_label.text = "Inventory: " + ", ".join([str(item) for item in inventory])
    enemy_count_label.text = "Enemies Destroyed: " + str(enemy_count)
    lives_count_label.text = "Lives Left: " + str(lives_count)
```

5. Instantiate the menu in the main game scene:
   - Open your main game scene (e.g., "Game.tscn").
   - Add a "CanvasLayer" node to the scene if you don't already have one.
   - Instance the "Menu.tscn" scene as a child of the "CanvasLayer" node.
   - In the main game script, create a reference to the menu instance:

```gdscript
onready var menu = $CanvasLayer/Menu
```

6. Update the menu with game data:
   - Whenever the inventory, enemy count, or lives count changes in your game, call the `update_menu` function on the menu instance and pass the updated values:

```gdscript
menu.update_menu(inventory, enemy_count, lives_count)
```

Now you have a basic menu that displays the inventory, enemy count, and lives count in your 2D platformer. You can further customize the appearance and functionality of the menu as needed.<#sep#>user: Quiero un relato para un niño de 5 años en el que se expliquen los principios básicos de las matemáticas

Érase una vez un oso panda que vivía en una cueva rodeado de bambú. El panda era muy goloso: ¡todos los días madrugaba para poder comerse todo el bambú que había crecido de noche antes que los otros pandas!

Sin embargo, por culpa del panda goloso, el resto de pandas tenían siempre mucha hambre.

- ¡Nunca hay comida porque ese panda rebelde se come todo el bambú! -se quejó uno.
    
- ¡Tenemos que hacer algo! -propuso otro.
    

No sabían qué hacer, hasta que un día se les ocurrió crear una regla para repartir los brotes de bambú entre todos.

Primero, tenían que contar cuántos brotes de bambú había cerca de la cueva. Así, los pandas aprendieron a contar y nacieron los números.

Pero había varias zonas diferentes, lo que complicó la tarea de los pandas. En una, había 5 brotes de bambú, mientras que en otra había 3, y en la última, 7. Los pandas se habían divido en varios grupos para contar cada zona por separado y así acabar antes; lo malo es que no sabían cuánto bambú había en total. Pero un panda muy inteligente dijo:

- Si tenemos tres zonas, con 5, 3 y 7 brotes, podemos contar el bambú de las tres y sumarlas. En la primera hay 5. Como en la segunda hay 3, contaremos desde 5 3 veces: el número siguiente al 5 es el 6, después, el 7, ¡y finalmente el 8!. Y como en la tercera hay 2, sumamos también esos 2 haciendo lo mismo. Como partimos de 8 y contamos 7: 9(1), 10(2), 11(3), 12(4), 13(5), 14(6), 15(7). Es por eso que 5 + 3 + 7 = 15. Así que tenemos 15 brotes de bambú -razonó.

Y así, los pandas aprendieron a sumar.

- ¡Que buena idea! -exclamó un panda.
    
- Sí. Lo malo es que he visto 1 brote de bambú que no se podía comer porque tenía muchos insectos... -dijo menos ilusionado otro panda.
    
- ¡Yo también! En mi zona he visto 2 brotes que tenían muy mala pinta. -añadió otro.
    
- No os preocupéis -respondió el panda inteligente-. Ya sabemos sumar. Si hay 1 brote no comestibles en una zona, y 2 en otra, en total hay 3 brotes que no se pueden comer de los 15 que existen.
    
- Sí, pero... ¿¡Entonces cuántos sí podemos comer!? -preguntó un panda muy curioso que tenía cada vez más hambre.
    
- Pues si hemos usado la suma para añadir al recuento de bambú los brotes de cada zona, ahora haremos lo contrario. ¡Usaremos la resta para quitar los que estén malos! -propuso emocionado el panda inteligente-. Si tenemos 15 en total -prosiguió- y 3 estropeados, podemos quitar esos 3 del total de 15 "contando" hacia atrás, es decir, restando. Tenemos que retroceder desde 15 3 veces: 14, 13, ¡y 12! ¡15 - 3 = 12 de bambú que sí podemos comer!
    

Y así, el grupo de pandas aprendió a restar.

Se pusieron entonces a contar cuántos pandas vivían en la cueva para poder repartir el bambú. Cada familia le dijo al panda inteligente cuántos eran. Una vez todos terminaron de informarlo, el panda inteligente dijo:

- Al parecer, en nuestra cueva hay 3 familias de 2 pandas, incluyéndome a mí. Así que si sumamos los 2 pandas 3 veces, sabremos cuántos somos en total -explicó-. ¿Puedes hacerlo por mí? - le pidió a un panda perezoso.
    
- Lo intentaré -respondió-. A ver... Tenemos 2 pandas + 2 pandas + 2 pandas así que hay...¡esta cuenta es muy larga y difícil!
    
- No te preocupes -le dijo el panda inteligente-. Como el 2 se repite 3 veces, usaremos la multiplicación. 2 x 3 = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 pandas.
    

Y así, los pandas aprendieron a multiplicar.

- ¡Genial! -aclamaron felices los pandas-. ¿Pero cómo podemos repartir los 95 brotes entre los 33 que vivimos en la cueva? -preguntaron. 
    
- Haremos lo contrario a multiplicar: dividir -explicó el panda inteligente-. Como somos 6 pandas y hay 15 de bambú, probaremos a multiplicar 6 por diferentes números hasta que nos de como resultado 15. Por ejemplo, 6 x 1 = 6. De esta forma, cada panda comería un brote de bambú, pero solo estaríamos comiendo 6 brotes en total, así que aún podemos comer más, y eso queremos, ¿no? Veamos si los brotes llegan para que cada panda coma 2. 6 x 2 = 12. Aún es menos que 15, así que no hay problema, ¡ningún panda se quedará sin comer! ¿Y 3? 6 x 3 = 18. Eso es demasiado, no tenemos tantos brotes... Es por ello que 15 : 6 = 2, que es lo que puede comer cada panda. Sin embargo, como nos comeremos 12 brotes, aún nos sobran 15 - 12 = 3 brotes. Ese es el resto de la división.
    
- Todo eso está muy bien -dijo el panda perezoso-. ¡Pero no podemos desperdiciar tantos brotes! ¿¡Es que has perdido la cabeza!?
    
- Claro que no. Como nos sobran 15, podemos dividir cada uno en trocitos más pequeños, y repartir también esos trozos. No solo podemos contar con números como el 1, el 2 o el 3, llamados naturales, sino también tener en cuenta esos trocitos usando números decimales como el 0,5, que sería medio brote porque es la mitad de uno, o el 1,5, que sería uno y medio. Como nos sobran 3 brotes, si dividimos cada uno en 2 mitades, tendremos 6 trozos, Y como somos 6 pandas, ¡cada panda tendrá un trozo de bambú extra aparte de sus 2 brotes! ¡Ese será el postre!
    

Así, los pandas aprendieron también a usar números decimales y, a partir de entonces, pudieron dividirse el bambú mucho mejor y conseguir que ninguno de ellos pasara hambre. El panda goloso ya no podía comer tanto, pero estaba feliz de ver a sus amigos contentos y con mucha energía. ¡Un final feliz para los pandas gracias a las matemáticas!

400 gramos de spaghetti

### Step 1: How should we make the game?

Well the best way for us to go about making the game would be to lay out the method here. In real life how would we play a game of memory. We'll think of each card as a playing card. We want to customize our images and make it easy to add more at any time, correct? So lets say all the cards constatute a deck. Here's how I recommend we go about starting the game.

1) Shuffle the deck
2) Take out X cards for the deck (a real deck would have 52, and make for a very, very long game. That's why we only use X cards total. This would also make it easy for us to make levels later on, incase we want to change X dynamically.).
3) Photocopy the retreived cards so we have perfect duplication (2 of each card).
4) Shuffle the duplicates (we can't have them be in the same order as our first set).
5) Lastly, deal the cards out from both decks at the same time.

 LOGIC MONSTER! Logic monster sez that ideally you'd want to deal them out randomly because otherwise someone could realize that if the decks were delt at the same time, there is no way N can match N + 2K, thus cutting possibles in HALF! But we'd like to think no one would notice this without knowing how it's programmed. It's not like they actually watched the cards get delt from both decks.

So does that sound like a reasonable form of getting cards and dealing them out? How can we make it more fun?

Now anyone can eventually get all the cards figured out, but it's our job to make the game fun. In that case, we'll keep track of the number of tries and time that occurs during play. This will allow us to get a scoring system, and then the game becomes more competative/interactive.

def is_palindrome(s):
    return s == s[::-1]

T = int(input())
for _ in range(T):
    s = input().strip()
    if is_palindrome(s):
        print("YES")
        continue
    left = 0
    right = len(s) - 1
    found = False
    while left < right:
        if s[left] == s[right]:
            left += 1
            right -= 1
        else:
            # Check two possibilities: delete left or delete right
            s1 = s[left+1 : right+1]  # Delete left character
            s2 = s[left : right]      # Delete right character
            if is_palindrome(s1) or is_palindrome(s2):
                print("YES")
            else:
                print("NO")
            found = True
            break
    if not found:
        print("YES")<#sep#>-

class FenwickTree:
    def __init__(self, size):
        self.n = size
        self.tree = [0] * (self.n + 2)

    def update(self, index, delta):
        while index <= self.n:
            self.tree[index] += delta
            index += index & -index

    def query(self, index):
        res = 0
        while index > 0:
            res += self.tree[index]
            index -= index & -index
        return res

n = int(input())
s = list(map(int, input().split()))
fenwick = FenwickTree(n)
for x in range(1, n+1):
    fenwick.update(x, x)

result = []
for i in range(n-1, -1, -1):
    current_s = s[i]
    low = 1
    high = n
    ans = -1
    while low <= high:
        mid = (low + high) // 2
        sum_mid_minus_1 = fenwick.query(mid - 1)
        if sum_mid_minus_1 < current_s:
            low = mid + 1
        elif sum_mid_minus_1 > current_s:
            high = mid - 1
        else:
            sum_mid = fenwick.query(mid)
            if sum_mid - sum_mid_minus_1 == mid:
                ans = mid
                break
            else:
                low = mid + 1
    result.append(ans)
    fenwick.update(ans, -ans)

result.reverse()
print(' '.join(map(str, result)))<#sep#>-

def convert_to_base(n, k):
    if n == 0:
        return '0'
    digits = []
    while n > 0:
        digits.append(str(n % k))
        n = n // k
    return ''.join(reversed(digits))

k = int(input())

for i in range(1, k):
    row = []
    for j in range(1, k):
        product = i * j
        row.append(convert_to_base(product, k))
    print(' '.join(row))<#sep#>-

import sys

def is_convex(points):
    cross = []
    for i in range(4):
        p = points[i]
        q = points[(i+1)%4]
        r = points[(i+2)%4]
        dx1 = q[0] - p[0]
        dy1 = q[1] - p[1]
        dx2 = r[0] - q[0]
        dy2 = r[1] - q[1]
        cross_val = dx1 * dy2 - dy1 * dx2
        cross.append(cross_val)
    if all(c >= 0 for c in cross) or all(c <= 0 for c in cross):
        return "YES"
    else:
        return "NO"

n, m = map(int, input().split())

if m == 0:
    print(0 if n == 1 else -1)
else:
    parent = list(range(n + 1))  # 1-based indexing

    def find(u):
        while parent[u] != u:
            parent[u] = parent[parent[u]]  # Path compression
            u = parent[u]
        return u

    def union(u, v):
        u_root = find(u)
        v_root = find(v)
        if u_root != v_root:
            parent[v_root] = u_root

    for _ in range(m):
        u, v, w = map(int, input().split())
        union(u, v)

    root = find(1)
    connected = True
    for i in range(2, n + 1):
        if find(i) != root:
            connected = False
            break

    print(n - 1 if connected else -1)<#sep#>-

def main():
    import sys
    input = sys.stdin.read().split('\n')
    idx = 0
    T = int(input[idx].strip())
    idx += 1
    for _ in range(T):
        # Read N, K, initial Answer
        while idx < len(input) and input[idx].strip() == '':
            idx += 1
        n, k, ans = map(int, input[idx].split())
        idx += 1
        # Read array A
        while idx < len(input) and input[idx].strip() == '':
            idx += 1
        a = list(map(int, input[idx].split()))
        idx += 1
        # Read operator
        while idx < len(input) and input[idx].strip() == '':
            idx += 1
        op = input[idx].strip()
        idx += 1
        
        # Compute cumulative value
        if op == 'AND':
            cum = a[0]
            for num in a[1:]:
                cum &= num
        elif op == 'OR':
            cum = a[0]
            for num in a[1:]:
                cum |= num
        elif op == 'XOR':
            cum = a[0]
            for num in a[1:]:
                cum ^= num
        
        # Compute result based on K and operator
        if k == 0:
            res = ans
        else:
            if op == 'AND':
                res = ans & cum
            elif op == 'OR':
                res = ans | cum
            elif op == 'XOR':
                if k % 2 == 1:
                    res = ans ^ cum
                else:
                    res = ans
        print(res)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()<#sep#>-

def main():
    import sys
    input = sys.stdin.read().split()
    m = int(input[0])
    n = int(input[1])
    grid = input[2:2+m]
    rows = m
    cols = len(grid[0]) if m > 0 else 0

    # Preprocess blocks
    visited = [[False for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)]
    block_map = [[None for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)]
    blocks = []
    for y in range(rows):
        for x in range(cols):
            if not visited[y][x] and grid[y][x] != '0':
                color = grid[y][x]
                # Determine y_end
                y_end = y
                while y_end + 1 < rows and grid[y_end + 1][x] == color:
                    y_end += 1
                # Determine x_end
                x_end = x
                while x_end + 1 < cols:
                    valid = True
                    for yy in range(y, y_end + 1):
                        if grid[yy][x_end + 1] != color:
                            valid = False
                            break
                    if valid:
                        x_end += 1
                    else:
                        break
                # Create block tuple (min_x, max_x, min_y, max_y, color)
                block = (x, x_end, y, y_end, color)
                blocks.append(block)
                # Mark visited and block_map
                for xx in range(x, x_end + 1):
                    for yy in range(y, y_end + 1):
                        visited[yy][xx] = True
                        block_map[yy][xx] = block

    # Initial state
    initial_block = block_map[0][0]
    current_block = initial_block
    dp = (1, 0)  # right
    cp = 'left'
    steps_done = 0
    states = {}
    found_cycle = False

    def rotate_clockwise(direction):
        dx, dy = direction
        if dx == 1:
            return (0, 1)
        elif dy == 1:
            return (-1, 0)
        elif dx == -1:
            return (0, -1)
        else:
            return (1, 0)

    def compute_exit_pixel(block, direction, cp_dir):
        min_x, max_x, min_y, max_y, _ = block
        dx, dy = direction
        if dx == 1:  # right
            x = max_x
            y = min_y if cp_dir == 'left' else max_y
        elif dx == -1:  # left
            x = min_x
            y = max_y if cp_dir == 'left' else min_y
        elif dy == 1:  # down
            y = max_y
            x = max_x if cp_dir == 'left' else min_x
        else:  # up
            y = min_y
            x = min_x if cp_dir == 'left' else max_x
        return (x, y)

    while steps_done < n:
        state_key = (current_block, dp, cp)
        if state_key in states:
            # Cycle detected
            cycle_start = states[state_key]
            cycle_length = steps_done - cycle_start
            remaining = (n - cycle_start) % cycle_length
            # Simulate remaining steps
            for _ in range(remaining):
                exit_x, exit_y = compute_exit_pixel(current_block, dp, cp)
                dx, dy = dp
                new_x = exit_x + dx
                new_y = exit_y + dy
                if 0 <= new_x < cols and 0 <= new_y < rows and grid[new_y][new_x] != '0':
                    current_block = block_map[new_y][new_x]
                else:
                    if cp == 'left':
                        cp = 'right'
                    else:
                        cp = 'left'
                        dp = rotate_clockwise(dp)
                steps_done += 1
            break
        else:
            states[state_key] = steps_done

        # Proceed with the current step
        exit_x, exit_y = compute_exit_pixel(current_block, dp, cp)
        dx, dy = dp
        new_x = exit_x + dx
        new_y = exit_y + dy

        if 0 <= new_x < cols and 0 <= new_y < rows and grid[new_y][new_x] != '0':
            current_block = block_map[new_y][new_x]
        else:
            if cp == 'left':
                cp = 'right'
            else:
                cp = 'left'
                dp = rotate_clockwise(dp)
        steps_done += 1

    print(current_block[4])

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()<#sep#>-

import sys
from itertools import combinations

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read().split()
    ptr = 0
    t = int(input[ptr])
    ptr += 1
    for _ in range(t):
        n, c, q = map(int, input[ptr:ptr+3])
        ptr +=3
        p = list(map(int, input[ptr:ptr+n]))
        ptr +=n
        queries = []
        for __ in range(q):
            i, j = map(int, input[ptr:ptr+2])
            ptr +=2
            queries.append( (i-1, j) )  # converting to 0-based index
        
        # Generate all possible interval combinations with cost sum <=c
        # Each interval is [l, r] with r-l >=1 (since cost >=1), and non-overlapping
        # Use BFS to generate all possible combinations
        from collections import deque
        
        # For BFS, each state is (current pos, remaining cost, intervals)
        # We start at pos 0, remaining cost c, and empty intervals
        # Each step, we can choose to skip current pos, or choose to reverse an interval starting at current pos
        # and then jump to the end of the interval +1
        
        # To avoid overlapping intervals, we track the end of the last interval
        # Modified BFS state: (current pos, remaining cost, list of intervals)
        # But this can be optimized by tracking current pos and remaining cost, and generating intervals accordingly
        # However, for the purposes of generating all possible combinations, we need to track the intervals
        
        # Initialize queue with no intervals
        queue = deque()
        queue.append( (0, c, []) )
        combinations_list = []
        
        while queue:
            pos, remaining, intervals = queue.popleft()
            if pos >=n:
                combinations_list.append(intervals)
                continue
            # Option 1: skip this position, move to pos+1
            queue.append( (pos+1, remaining, intervals.copy()) )
            # Option 2: choose to reverse an interval starting at pos with cost m (m >=1)
            for m in range(1, remaining+1):
                # cost m corresponds to length m+1 (r-l =m)
                end = pos + m
                if end >=n:
                    continue
                # Check that this interval is valid
                new_intervals = intervals.copy()
                new_intervals.append( (pos, end) )
                new_remaining = remaining - m
                queue.append( (end+1, new_remaining, new_intervals) )
        
        # Now apply all combinations and collect unique permutations
        seen = set()
        unique_permutations = []
        original = tuple(p)
        seen.add(original)
        unique_permutations.append(original)
        
        for intervals in combinations_list:
            # Apply the intervals to the original permutation
            tmp = list(p)
            for l, r in intervals:
                # Reverse [l, r]
                while l < r:
                    tmp[l], tmp[r] = tmp[r], tmp[l]
                    l +=1
                    r -=1
            perm = tuple(tmp)
            if perm not in seen:
                seen.add(perm)
                unique_permutations.append(perm)
        
        # Sort the unique permutations lex order
        unique_permutations.sort()
        
        # Answer queries
        total = len(unique_permutations)
        for i, j in queries:
            if j > total:
                print(-1)
            else:
                print(unique_permutations[j-1][i])
                
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()<#sep#>-

a_doubled = a * 2  # Handle circular sequences

current_len = 0
prev_adjusted = -1  # Initialize to a value lower than any possible position (0 to lb-1)

for x in a_doubled:
    if x not in pos_in_b:
        current_len = 0
        prev_adjusted = -1
        continue
    
    pos = pos_in_b[x]
    
    if current_len == 0:
        current_len = 1
        prev_adjusted = pos
    else:
        if pos > prev_adjusted:
            adjusted_pos = pos
        else:
            adjusted_pos = pos + lb
        
        if adjusted_pos > prev_adjusted:
            current_len += 1
            prev_adjusted = adjusted_pos
        else:
            current_len = 1
            prev_adjusted = pos
    
    if current_len > max_len:
        max_len = current_len
    
    if max_len >= lb:
        break  # Early exit if maximum possible is found

from collections import deque

x0, y0, x1, y1 = map(int, input().split())
n = int(input())

allowed_rows = {}
for _ in range(n):
    ri, ai, bi = map(int, input().split())
    if ri not in allowed_rows:
        allowed_rows[ri] = []
    allowed_rows[ri].append((ai, bi))

allowed_rows_processed = {}
for r in allowed_rows:
    intervals = allowed_rows[r]
    intervals.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
    merged = []
    for interval in intervals:
        a, b = interval
        if not merged:
            merged.append((a, b))
        else:
            last_a, last_b = merged[-1]
            if a <= last_b + 1:
                merged[-1] = (last_a, max(last_b, b))
            else:
                merged.append((a, b))
    starts = [interval[0] for interval in merged]
    allowed_rows_processed[r] = (merged, starts)

allowed_rows = allowed_rows_processed

start = (x0, y0)
end = (x1, y1)

dist = {start: 0}
queue = deque([start])

found = False
while queue:
    current = queue.popleft()
    x, y = current
    if current == end:
        print(dist[current])
        exit()
    for dx in (-1, 0, 1):
        for dy in (-1, 0, 1):
            if dx == 0 and dy == 0:
                continue
            nx = x + dx
            ny = y + dy
            neighbor = (nx, ny)
            if nx not in allowed_rows:
                continue
            merged, starts = allowed_rows[nx]
            idx = bisect.bisect_right(starts, ny) - 1
            if idx >= 0 and merged[idx][1] >= ny:
                if neighbor not in dist:
                    dist[neighbor] = dist[current] + 1
                    queue.append(neighbor)
                    if neighbor == end:

    if count_b[ch] == 0:

# Compute prefix sums and max_gap

    current_sum += d
    prefix.append(current_sum)

# Coefficients for perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC
A1 = 2 * (bx - ax)
B1 = 2 * (by - ay)
C1 = (ax**2 + ay**2) - (bx**2 + by**2)

A2 = 2 * (cx - bx)
B2 = 2 * (cy - by)
C2 = (bx**2 + by**2) - (cx**2 + cy**2)

# Calculate determinant for line intersection
D = A1 * B2 - A2 * B1

if D != 0:
    # Calculate intersection point O
    x = (B1 * C2 - B2 * C1) / D
    y = (A2 * C1 - A1 * C2) / D

    # Vectors from O to A, B, C
    oax = ax - x
    oay = ay - y
    obx = bx - x
    oby = by - y
    ocx = cx - x
    ocy = cy - y

    # Check if all distances from O are equal
    oa_sq = oax**2 + oay**2
    ob_sq = obx**2 + oby**2
    oc_sq = ocx**2 + ocy**2

    if not (oa_sq == ob_sq and ob_sq == oc_sq):
        print("No")
    else:
        # Calculate cross and dot products
        cross1 = oax * oby - oay * obx
        cross2 = obx * ocy - oby * ocx
        dot1 = oax * obx + oay * oby
        dot2 = obx * ocx + oby * ocy

        # Check angle and direction conditions
        if cross1 * cross2 < 0 or cross1 * dot2 != cross2 * dot1:
            print("No")
        else:
            print("Yes")
else:
    # Check if lines are the same
    if A1 * C2 != A2 * C1 or B1 * C2 != B2 * C1:
        print("No")

import sys

MAX_VALUE_STR = '1000000000000'

def is_valid_part(s_part):
    if len(s_part) == 0:
        return False
    if len(s_part) > 13:
        return False
    if len(s_part) > 1 and s_part[0] == '0':
        return False
    if len(s_part) == 13:
        return s_part == MAX_VALUE_STR
    return True

def part_to_num(s_part):
    if len(s_part) == 13:
        return 10**12
    return int(s_part)

def process_string(s):
    L = len(s)
    if L < 4:
        return "unlucky"
    max_sum = -1
    max_a = L - 3
    for a in range(1, max_a + 1):
        max_b = L - 2
        for b in range(a + 1, max_b + 1):
            max_c = L - 1
            for c in range(b + 1, max_c + 1):
                p1 = s[0:a]
                p2 = s[a:b]
                p3 = s[b:c]
                p4 = s[c:L]
                valid = is_valid_part(p1) and is_valid_part(p2) and is_valid_part(p3) and is_valid_part(p4)
                if not valid:
                    continue
                current_sum = part_to_num(p1) + part_to_num(p2) + part_to_num(p3) + part_to_num(p4)
                if current_sum > max_sum:
                    max_sum = current_sum
    return max_sum if max_sum != -1 else "unlucky"

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read().split()
    N = int(input[0])
    for i in range(1, N + 1):
        s = input[i].strip()
        print(process_string(s))

import math

def compute_intervals(a_seg, b_seg, R):
    a_t_start, a_t_end, a_vx, a_vy, a_x0, a_y0 = a_seg
    b_t_start, b_t_end, b_vx, b_vy, b_x0, b_y0 = b_seg

    t_start = max(a_t_start, b_t_start)
    t_end = min(a_t_end, b_t_end)
    if t_start >= t_end:
        return []

    a = a_vx - b_vx
    c1 = (a_x0 - b_x0) - a_vx * a_t_start + b_vx * b_t_start
    b_coeff = a_vy - b_vy
    c2 = (a_y0 - b_y0) - a_vy * a_t_start + b_vy * b_t_start

    A = a**2 + b_coeff**2
    B = 2 * (a * c1 + b_coeff * c2)
    C = c1**2 + c2**2 - R**2

    if A == 0:
        if B == 0:
            return [(t_start, t_end)] if C <= 0 else []
        else:
            t0 = -C / B
            if B > 0:
                s = t_start
                e = min(t_end, t0)
            else:
                s = max(t_start, t0)
                e = t_end
            return [(s, e)] if s <= e else []
    else:
        D = B**2 - 4 * A * C
        if D < 0:
            return []
        sqrt_D = math.sqrt(D)
        t1 = (-B - sqrt_D) / (2 * A)
        t2 = (-B + sqrt_D) / (2 * A)
        if t1 > t2:
            t1, t2 = t2, t1
        s = max(t_start, t1)
        e = min(t_end, t2)
        return [(s, e)] if s <= e else []

def main():
    import sys
    input = sys.stdin.read().split('\n')
    ptr = 0
    while True:
        while ptr < len(input) and not input[ptr].strip():
            ptr += 1
        if ptr >= len(input):
            break
        line = input[ptr].strip()
        if line == '0 0 0':
            break
        N, T, R = map(int, line.split())
        ptr += 1
        robots = []
        nick_to_idx = {}
        for _ in range(N):
            while ptr < len(input) and not input[ptr].strip():
                ptr += 1
            nickname = input[ptr].strip()
            ptr += 1
            seg_lines = []
            while True:
                while ptr < len(input) and not input[ptr].strip():
                    ptr += 1
                if ptr >= len(input):
                    break
                line = input[ptr].strip()
                ptr += 1
                parts = line.split()
                if not parts:
                    continue
                t = int(parts[0])
                if t == T and seg_lines:
                    seg_lines.append((t, int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])))
                    break
                seg_lines.append((t, int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])))
                if t == T:
                    break
            t0, x0, y0 = seg_lines[0][0], seg_lines[0][1], seg_lines[0][2]
            segments = []
            prev_t = t0
            x = x0
            y = y0
            for i in range(1, len(seg_lines)):
                t, vx, vy = seg_lines[i]
                segments.append((prev_t, t, vx, vy, x, y))
                dt = t - prev_t
                x += dt * vx
                y += dt * vy
                prev_t = t
            robots.append((nickname, segments))
            nick_to_idx[nickname] = len(robots) - 1
        intervals = []
        for i in range(N):
            for j in range(i + 1, N):
                for a_seg in robots[i][1]:
                    for b_seg in robots[j][1]:
                        ivals = compute_intervals(a_seg, b_seg, R)
                        for ival in ivals:
                            s, e = ival
                            intervals.append((s, e, i, j))
        intervals.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
        data_time = [float('inf')] * N
        data_time[0] = 0.0
        for s, e, i, j in intervals:
            e = min(e, T)
            if s > e:
                continue
            if data_time[i] <= e:
                possible = max(s, data_time[i])
                if possible <= e and data_time[j] > possible:
                    data_time[j] = possible
            if data_time[j] <= e:
                possible = max(s, data_time[j])
                if possible <= e and data_time[i] > possible:
                    data_time[i] = possible
        result = []
        for idx in range(N):
            if data_time[idx] <= T:
                result.append(robots[idx][0])
        result.sort()
        for name in result:
            print(name)

import sys

def readints():
    return list(map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split()))

def polygon_area(points):
    area = 0.0
    n = len(points)
    for i in range(n):
        j = (i + 1) % n
        area += points[i][0] * points[j][1] - points[i][1] * points[j][0]
    return abs(area) / 2.0

def sutherland_hodgman(subject_polygon, clip_edge):
    def inside(p):
        a, b, c = clip_edge
        return a * p[0] + b * p[1] + c >= 0

    def compute_intersection(s, e):
        a, b, c = clip_edge
        x1, y1 = s
        x2, y2 = e
        denom = a * (x2 - x1) + b * (y2 - y1)
        if denom == 0:
            return None
        t = -(a * x1 + b * y1 + c) / denom
        if t < 0 or t > 1:
            return None
        x = x1 + t * (x2 - x1)
        y = y1 + t * (y2 - y1)
        return (x, y)

    if not subject_polygon:
        return []
    output_list = []
    s = subject_polygon[-1]
    for e in subject_polygon:
        if inside(e):
            if not inside(s):
                intersection = compute_intersection(s, e)
                if intersection:
                    output_list.append(intersection)
            output_list.append(e)
        else:
            if inside(s):
                intersection = compute_intersection(s, e)
                if intersection:
                    output_list.append(intersection)
        s = e
    return output_list

def main():
    H, W = readints()
    mA1, mA2, mB1, mB2, mX = readints()
    grid = []
    for _ in range(H):
        grid.append(sys.stdin.readline().strip())

    # Precompute counts and sums for each type
    count_A = 0
    sum_x_A = 0.0
    sum_y_A = 0.0
    count_B = 0
    sum_x_B = 0.0
    sum_y_B = 0.0
    count_X = 0
    sum_x_X = 0.0
    sum_y_X = 0.0
    non_empty = []

    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            c = grid[i][j]
            if c == '.':
                continue
            non_empty.append((i, j))
            x = i + 0.5
            y = j + 0.5
            if c == 'A':
                count_A += 1
                sum_x_A += x
                sum_y_A += y
            elif c == 'B':
                count_B += 1
                sum_x_B += x
                sum_y_B += y
            elif c == 'X':
                count_X += 1
                sum_x_X += x * mX
                sum_y_X += y * mX

    C = count_X * mX
    D = sum_x_X
    E = sum_y_X

    # Check if any cell covers the entire domain
    for (i, j) in non_empty:
        # Compute the four constraints for this cell
        # X lower: a1*A + b1*B + c1 >= 0
        a1 = sum_x_A - i * count_A
        b1 = sum_x_B - i * count_B
        c1 = D - i * C

        # X upper: a2*A + b2*B + c2 < 0
        a2 = sum_x_A - (i+1)*count_A
        b2 = sum_x_B - (i+1)*count_B
        c2 = D - (i+1)*C

        # Y lower: a3*A + b3*B + c3 >= 0
        a3 = sum_y_A - j * count_A
        b3 = sum_y_B - j * count_B
        c3 = E - j * C

        # Y upper: a4*A + b4*B + c4 < 0
        a4 = sum_y_A - (j+1)*count_A
        b4 = sum_y_B - (j+1)*count_B
        c4 = E - (j+1)*C

        # Check if all four constraints are satisfied for all corners
        corners = [
            (mA1, mB1),
            (mA1, mB2),
            (mA2, mB1),
            (mA2, mB2)
        ]
        all_x_lower = all(a1*A + b1*B + c1 >= 0 for (A, B) in corners)
        all_x_upper = all(a2*A + b2*B + c2 < 0 for (A, B) in corners)
        all_y_lower = all(a3*A + b3*B + c3 >= 0 for (A, B) in corners)
        all_y_upper = all(a4*A + b4*B + c4 < 0 for (A, B) in corners)

        if all_x_lower and all_x_upper and all_y_lower and all_y_upper:
            print("1.0")
            return

    # If no cell covers the entire domain, compute feasible regions for each cell
    total_area = 0.0
    domain_area = (mA2 - mA1) * (mB2 - mB1)
    if domain_area == 0:
        print("0.0")
        return

    for (i, j) in non_empty:
        a1 = sum_x_A - i * count_A
        b1 = sum_x_B - i * count_B
        c1 = D - i * C
        x_lower = (a1, b1, c1)

        a2 = sum_x_A - (i+1)*count_A
        b2 = sum_x_B - (i+1)*count_B
        c2 = D - (i+1)*C
        x_upper = (a2, b2, c2)

        a3 = sum_y_A - j * count_A
        b3 = sum_y_B - j * count_B
        c3 = E - j * C
        y_lower = (a3, b3, c3)

        a4 = sum_y_A - (j+1)*count_A
        b4 = sum_y_B - (j+1)*count_B
        c4 = E - (j+1)*C
        y_upper = (a4, b4, c4)

        edges = [x_lower, x_upper, y_lower, y_upper]
        clipped_polygon = [(mA1, mB1), (mA1, mB2), (mA2, mB2), (mA2, mB1)]

        for edge in edges:
            clipped_polygon = sutherland_hodgman(clipped_polygon, edge)
            if not clipped_polygon:
                break

        if clipped_polygon:
            area = polygon_area(clipped_polygon)
            total_area += area

    probability = total_area / domain_area
    print("{0:.12f}".format(probability))

import sys
from collections import defaultdict

def main():
    n, m = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
    rows = [sys.stdin.readline().strip() for _ in range(n)]
    
    freq = defaultdict(int)
    for j in range(m):
        c = 0
        for i in range(n):
            if rows[i][j] == '1':
                c |= 1 << i
        freq[c] += 1
    
    max_mask = (1 << n) - 1
    bit_count = [0] * (max_mask + 1)
    for x in range(max_mask + 1):
        bit_count[x] = bin(x).count('1')
    
    min_total = float('inf')
    for mask in range(max_mask + 1):
        total = 0
        for c, cnt in freq.items():
            xor = c ^ mask
            a = bit_count[xor]
            total += min(a, n - a) * cnt
        if total < min_total:
            min_total = total
    print(min_total)

import sys
from collections import deque

def main():
    n, m = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for _ in range(m):
        u, v = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
        adj[u].append(v)
        adj[v].append(u)
    
    color = [-1] * (n + 1)
    possible = True
    
    for u in range(1, n + 1):
        if color[u] == -1:
            if not adj[u]:
                color[u] = 0
                continue
            queue = deque([u])
            color[u] = 0
            while queue:
                current = queue.popleft()
                for neighbor in adj[current]:
                    if color[neighbor] == -1:
                        color[neighbor] = 1 - color[current]
                        queue.append(neighbor)
                    elif color[neighbor] == color[current]:
                        possible = False
                        break
                if not possible:
                    break
            if not possible:
                break
    
    if not possible:
        print(-1)
    else:
        a = [i for i in range(1, n + 1) if color[i] == 0]
        b = [i for i in range(1, n + 1) if color[i] == 1]
        print(len(a))
        print(' '.join(map(str, a)))
        print(len(b))
        print(' '.join(map(str, b)))

def left_rotate_1(s):
    if len(s) <= 1:
        return s
    return s[1:] + s[0]

def right_rotate_1(s):
    if len(s) <= 1:
        return s
    return s[-1] + s[:-1]

def swap_halves(s):
    n = len(s)
    if n % 2 == 0:
        mid = n // 2
        return s[mid:] + s[:mid]
    else:
        mid = n // 2
        return s[mid+1:] + s[mid] + s[:mid]

def decrement_digits(s):
    res = []
    for c in s:
        if c.isdigit():
            res.append(str((int(c) - 1) % 10))
        else:
            res.append(c)
    return ''.join(res)

def increment_digits(s):
    res = []
    for c in s:
        if c.isdigit():
            res.append(str((int(c) + 1) % 10))
        else:
            res.append(c)
    return ''.join(res)

def is_prime(n):
    if n < 2:
        return False
    if n == 2:
        return True
    if n % 2 == 0:
        return False
    max_divisor = int(n ** 0.5) + 1
    for i in range(3, max_divisor, 2):
        if n % i == 0:
            return False
    return True

            n = n // 2

            while n % i == 0:

                n = n // i

        return factors

import sys
from collections import deque

def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(1 << 25)
    n = int(sys.stdin.readline())
    edges = []
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n+1)]
    initial_t = [0] * (n)  # 1-based to n-1
    for i in range(n-1):
        u, v, t = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
        edges.append((u, v))
        adj[u].append((v, i+1))
        adj[v].append((u, i+1))
        initial_t[i+1] = t

    # Root the tree at 1, compute parent and child relationships
    parent = [0]*(n+1)
    children = [[] for _ in range(n+1)]
    edge_id_to_child = {}  # edge id to child node
    q = deque()
    q.append(1)
    visited = [False]*(n+1)
    visited[1] = True
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        for v, eid in adj[u]:
            if not visited[v]:
                visited[v] = True
                parent[v] = u
                children[u].append(v)
                edge_id_to_child[eid] = v
                q.append(v)

    # Compute initial parity for each node (sum of t along path from root)
    initial_parity = [0]*(n+1)
    q = deque()
    q.append(1)
    visited = [False]*(n+1)
    visited[1] = True
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        for v, eid in children[u]:
            initial_parity[v] = initial_parity[u] ^ initial_t[eid]
            visited[v] = True
            q.append(v)

    # Euler Tour to get in and out times
    in_time = [0]*(n+1)
    out_time = [0]*(n+1)
    time = 0
    stack = [(1, False)]
    while stack:
        u, visited = stack.pop()
        if visited:
            out_time[u] = time
            continue
        time += 1
        in_time[u] = time
        stack.append((u, True))
        for v in reversed(children[u]):
            stack.append((v, False))

    # Fenwick Tree for range XOR and point query
    class FenwickTree:
        def __init__(self, size):
            self.n = size
            self.tree = [0]*(self.n + 2)
        
        def update(self, idx, val=1):
            while idx <= self.n:
                self.tree[idx] ^= val
                idx += idx & -idx
        
        def range_xor(self, l, r):
            self.update(l)
            self.update(r+1)
        
        def query(self, idx):
            res = 0
            while idx > 0:
                res ^= self.tree[idx]
                idx -= idx & -idx
            return res
    
    ft = FenwickTree(n)

    def get_parity(u):
        return initial_parity[u] ^ ft.query(in_time[u])

    def bfs(start_parity):
        max_dist = -1
        far_node = start_parity[0]
        q = deque()
        visited = {}
        q.append((far_node, -1, 0))
        visited[far_node] = 0
        while q:
            u, parent_u, dist = q.popleft()
            for v, eid in adj[u]:
                if v == parent_u:
                    continue
                current_p = get_parity(v)
                if current_p != start_parity[1]:
                    continue
                if v not in visited or dist + 1 > visited[v]:
                    visited[v] = dist + 1
                    q.append((v, u, dist + 1))
                    if visited[v] > max_dist:
                        max_dist = visited[v]
                        far_node = v
        return far_node, max_dist

    m = int(sys.stdin.readline())
    for _ in range(m):
        eid = int(sys.stdin.readline())
        child_v = edge_id_to_child[eid]
        l = in_time[child_v]
        r = out_time[child_v]
        ft.range_xor(l, r)

        # Get current parity for all nodes
        # This is not feasible for large n, but works for the sample
        # For large n, this part needs optimization
        current_parities = [get_parity(u) for u in range(1, n+1)]
        group0 = [u for u in range(1, n+1) if current_parities[u-1] == 0]
        group1 = [u for u in range(1, n+1) if current_parities[u-1] == 1]
        if not group0 and not group1:
            print(0)
            continue
        max_len = 0
        for group in [group0, group1]:
            if len(group) < 1:
                continue
            start = group[0]
            u, _ = bfs((start, group[0]%2))
            v, dist = bfs((u, get_parity(u)))
            if dist > max_len:
                max_len = dist
        print(max_len if max_len != 0 else 0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()<#sep#>-

import heapq

n, m, k = map(int, input().split())
a = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
important = []
for _ in range(k):
    x, y = map(int, input().split())
    important.append((x-1, y-1))

index_map = {(x, y): i for i, (x, y) in enumerate(important)}

INF = float('inf')
dirs = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
full_mask = (1 << k) - 1

# Initialize distance and predecessor arrays
dist = [[[INF] * (1 << k) for _ in range(m)] for __ in range(n)]
prev = [[[None] * (1 << k) for _ in range(m)] for __ in range(n)]
heap = []

for idx, (x, y) in enumerate(important):
    mask = 1 << idx
    dist[x][y][mask] = a[x][y]
    heapq.heappush(heap, (a[x][y], x, y, mask))

while heap:
    cost, x, y, mask = heapq.heappop(heap)
    if mask == full_mask:
        break
    if cost > dist[x][y][mask]:
        continue
    for dx, dy in dirs:
        nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
        if 0 <= nx < n and 0 <= ny < m:
            new_mask = mask
            if (nx, ny) in index_map:
                new_mask |= 1 << index_map[(nx, ny)]
            new_cost = cost + a[nx][ny]
            if new_cost < dist[nx][ny][new_mask]:
                dist[nx][ny][new_mask] = new_cost
                prev[nx][ny][new_mask] = (x, y, mask)
                heapq.heappush(heap, (new_cost, nx, ny, new_mask))

min_cost = INF
best_x, best_y = -1, -1
for x in range(n):
    for y in range(m):
        if dist[x][y][full_mask] < min_cost:
            min_cost = dist[x][y][full_mask]
            best_x, best_y = x, y

current_x, current_y, current_mask = best_x, best_y, full_mask

    if p is None:
        break
    px, py, prev_mask = p
    current_x, current_y, current_mask = px, py, prev_mask

def are_equivalent(a, b):
    if a == b:
        return True
    n = len(a)
    if n % 2 != 0:
        return False
    if sorted(a) != sorted(b):
        return False
    mid = n // 2
    a1, a2 = a[:mid], a[mid:]
    b1, b2 = b[:mid], b[mid:]
    return (are_equivalent(a1, b1) and are_equivalent(a2, b2)) or (are_equivalent(a1, b2) and are_equivalent(a2, b1))

from collections import deque, defaultdict

def min_jumps(start, end, color_map, colors):
    if start == end:
        return 0
    N = len(colors)
    visited = [False] * N
    processed_colors = set()
    q = deque([(start, 0)])
    visited[start] = True
    
    while q:
        pos, dist = q.popleft()
        if pos == end:
            return dist
        # Move left
        if pos > 0 and not visited[pos - 1]:
            visited[pos - 1] = True
            q.append((pos - 1, dist + 1))
        # Process same color
        current_color = colors[pos]
        if current_color not in processed_colors:
            processed_colors.add(current_color)
            for neighbor in color_map[current_color]:
                if not visited[neighbor]:
                    visited[neighbor] = True
                    q.append((neighbor, dist + 1))
    return -1

    import sys

    Q = int(input[ptr])
    ptr += 1
    for _ in range(Q):
        S = int(input[ptr])
        M = int(input[ptr + 1])
        E = int(input[ptr + 2])
        ptr += 3
        # Compute S to M
        if S == M:
            part1 = 0
        else:
            part1 = min_jumps(S, M, color_map, colors)
        if part1 == -1:
            print(-1)
            continue
        # Compute M to E
        if M == E:
            part2 = 0
        else:
            part2 = min_jumps(M, E, color_map, colors)
        if part2 == -1:
            print(-1)
        else:
            print(part1 + part2)

def count_trailing_zeros(n):

import sys
from collections import deque

class Edge:
    def __init__(self, to, rev, cap):
        self.to = to
        self.rev = rev
        self.cap = cap

class Dinic:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.size = n
        self.graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    
    def add_edge(self, fr, to, cap):
        forward = Edge(to, len(self.graph[to]), cap)
        backward = Edge(fr, len(self.graph[fr]), 0)
        self.graph[fr].append(forward)
        self.graph[to].append(backward)
    
    def bfs_level(self, s, t, level):
        q = deque()
        level[:] = [-1] * self.size
        level[s] = 0
        q.append(s)
        while q:
            v = q.popleft()
            for edge in self.graph[v]:
                if edge.cap > 0 and level[edge.to] == -1:
                    level[edge.to] = level[v] + 1
                    q.append(edge.to)
                    if edge.to == t:
                        return
    
    def dfs_flow(self, v, t, upTo, iter_, level):
        if v == t:
            return upTo
        for i in range(iter_[v], len(self.graph[v])):
            edge = self.graph[v][i]
            if edge.cap > 0 and level[v] < level[edge.to]:
                d = self.dfs_flow(edge.to, t, min(upTo, edge.cap), iter_, level)
                if d > 0:
                    edge.cap -= d
                    self.graph[edge.to][edge.rev].cap += d
                    return d
            iter_[v] += 1
        return 0
    
    def max_flow(self, s, t):
        flow = 0
        level = [-1] * self.size
        while True:
            self.bfs_level(s, t, level)
            if level[t] == -1:
                return flow
            iter_ = [0] * self.size
            while True:
                f = self.dfs_flow(s, t, float('inf'), iter_, level)
                if f == 0:
                    break
                flow += f

import sys

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read().split()
    idx = 0
    n = int(input[idx]); idx +=1
    m = int(input[idx]); idx +=1
    r = int(input[idx]); idx +=1

    # Precompute distance matrices for each car using Floyd-Warshall
    dist = []
    for _ in range(m):
        d = []
        for i in range(n):
            row = list(map(int, input[idx:idx+n]))
            idx +=n
            d.append(row.copy())
        # Floyd-Warshall
        for k in range(n):
            for i in range(n):
                for j in range(n):
                    if d[i][k] + d[k][j] < d[i][j]:
                        d[i][j] = d[i][k] + d[k][j]
        dist.append(d)

    for _ in range(r):
        s = int(input[idx])-1; idx +=1
        t = int(input[idx])-1; idx +=1
        ki = int(input[idx]); idx +=1
        s_max = min(ki + 1, m)
        
        # Initialize for seg=1
        prev_dp = [ [dist[c][s][u] for u in range(n)] for c in range(m) ]
        ans = min(prev_dp[c][t] for c in range(m))
        if s_max == 1:
            print(ans)
            continue
        
        for seg in range(2, s_max + 1):
            # Compute min1 and min2 for each city v
            min1_val = [float('inf')] * n
            min1_car = [-1] * n
            min2_val = [float('inf')] * n
            for v in range(n):
                min1 = float('inf')
                min1_c = -1
                min2 = float('inf')
                for c in range(m):
                    val = prev_dp[c][v]
                    if val < min1:
                        min2 = min1
                        min1 = val
                        min1_c = c
                    elif val < min2:
                        min2 = val
                min1_val[v] = min1
                min1_car[v] = min1_c
                min2_val[v] = min2
            
            # Compute current_dp
            current_dp = [ [float('inf')] * n for _ in range(m) ]
            for c in range(m):
                prev_min = []
                for v in range(n):
                    if min1_car[v] != c:
                        prev_min.append(min1_val[v])
                    else:
                        prev_min.append(min2_val[v])
                
                for u in range(n):
                    min_total = min( prev_min[v] + dist[c][v][u] for v in range(n) )
                    current_dp[c][u] = min_total
            
            # Update answer
            current_ans = min(current_dp[c][t] for c in range(m))
            if current_ans < ans:
                ans = current_ans
            prev_dp = current_dp
        
        print(ans)

import bisect

class SegmentTree:
    def __init__(self, size, default_val):
        self.n = 1
        while self.n < size:
            self.n <<= 1
        self.size = self.n
        self.data = [default_val] * (2 * self.n)
        self.default_val = default_val

    def update(self, idx, value):
        idx += self.n
        if self.data[idx] < value:
            self.data[idx] = value
            idx >>= 1
            while idx >= 1:
                new_val = max(self.data[2 * idx], self.data[2 * idx + 1])
                if self.data[idx] == new_val:
                    break
                self.data[idx] = new_val
                idx >>= 1

    def query_max(self, l, r):
        res = self.default_val
        l += self.n
        r += self.n
        while l <= r:
            if l % 2 == 1:
                res = max(res, self.data[l])
                l += 1
            if r % 2 == 0:
                res = max(res, self.data[r])
                r -= 1
            l >>= 1
            r >>= 1
        return res

def main():
    import sys
    input = sys.stdin.read().split()
    ptr = 0
    N = int(input[ptr])
    ptr += 1
    B = list(map(int, input[ptr:ptr+N]))
    ptr += N
    I = list(map(int, input[ptr:ptr+N]))
    ptr += N
    R = list(map(int, input[ptr:ptr+N]))

    ladies = list(zip(B, I, R))
    ladies_sorted = sorted(ladies, key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1], x[2]))

    groups = []
    current_B = None
    current_group = []
    for lady in ladies_sorted:
        if lady[0] != current_B:
            if current_group:
                groups.append(current_group)
            current_group = [lady]
            current_B = lady[0]
        else:
            current_group.append(lady)
    if current_group:
        groups.append(current_group)

    all_I = [lady[1] for lady in ladies]
    sorted_I = sorted(list(set(all_I)))
    sorted_I.sort()

    if not sorted_I:
        print(0)
        return

    st = SegmentTree(len(sorted_I), -1)
    answer = 0

    for group in groups:
        for (b, i, r) in group:
            pos = bisect.bisect_right(sorted_I, i)
            if pos < len(sorted_I):
                max_r = st.query_max(pos, len(sorted_I) - 1)
                if max_r > r:
                    answer += 1

        i_max = {}
        for (b, i, r) in group:
            if i in i_max:
                if r > i_max[i]:
                    i_max[i] = r
            else:
                i_max[i] = r

        for i in i_max:
            r = i_max[i]
            idx = bisect.bisect_left(sorted_I, i)
            current_max = st.query_max(idx, idx)
            if r > current_max:
                st.update(idx, r)

    print(answer)

import sys
from collections import deque

def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(1 << 25)
    N, M = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
    D = list(map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split()))
    edges = []
    for _ in range(M):
        u, v = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
        edges.append((u-1, v-1))  # 0-based
    
    color = [-1] * N  # 0: B, 1: W
    adj_eq = [[] for _ in range(N)]
    conflict = False

    # Process edges with D[u] != D[v]
    for u, v in edges:
        if D[u] > D[v]:
            # u must be B (0), v must be W (1)
            if color[u] == 1 or color[v] == 0:
                conflict = True
            if color[u] == -1:
                color[u] = 0
            if color[v] == -1:
                color[v] = 1
            if color[u] != 0 or color[v] != 1:
                conflict = True
        elif D[u] < D[v]:
            # u must be W (1), v must be B (0)
            if color[u] == 0 or color[v] == 1:
                conflict = True
            if color[u] == -1:
                color[u] = 1
            if color[v] == -1:
                color[v] = 0
            if color[u] != 1 or color[v] != 0:
                conflict = True
        else:
            adj_eq[u].append(v)
            adj_eq[v].append(u)
    
    if conflict:
        print(-1)
        return
    
    # Process edges with D[u] == D[v], forming a bipartition graph
    # Now assign colors for nodes not yet colored, ensuring bipartition
    # Use BFS
    for i in range(N):
        if color[i] == -1:
            # Assign color 0 if possible
            color[i] = 0
            q = deque()
            q.append(i)
            while q:
                u = q.popleft()
                for v in adj_eq[u]:
                    if color[v] == -1:
                        color[v] = 1 - color[u]
                        q.append(v)
                    elif color[v] == color[u]:
                        print(-1)
                        return
    
    # Check all equality edges
    for u, v in edges:
        if D[u] == D[v]:
            if color[u] == color[v]:
                print(-1)
                return
    
    # Now check if all nodes have at least one neighbor of opposite color
    # Also check the minimal edge weight for each node
    adj_colors = [[] for _ in range(N)]  # list of (color, D of other)
    for u, v in edges:
        if color[u] != color[v]:
            adj_colors[u].append(D[v])
            adj_colors[v].append(D[u])
    
    has_black = False
    has_white = False
    for i in range(N):
        if color[i] == 0:
            has_black = True
        else:
            has_white = True
        if not adj_colors[i]:
            print(-1)
            return
        min_d = min(adj_colors[i])
        if color[i] == 0 and min_d != D[i]:
            print(-1)
            return
        if color[i] == 1 and min_d != D[i]:
            print(-1)
            return
    
    if not has_black or not has_white:
        print(-1)
        return
    
    # Assign edge weights
    output_edges = []
    for u, v in edges:
        if color[u] != color[v]:
            output_edges.append(max(D[u], D[v]))
        else:
            output_edges.append(10**9)
    
    # Generate output
    s = ''.join(['B' if c == 0 else 'W' for c in color])
    print(s)
    for c in output_edges:
        print(c)

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read

    idx +=2
    edges = [[] for _ in range(n+1)]
    parent = [0]*(n+1)
    depth = [0]*(n+1)
    for i in range(2, n+1):
        p = int(data[idx])
        w = int(data[idx+1])
        idx +=2
        parent[i] = p
        edges[p].append(i)
        depth[i] = depth[p] + w
    for u in range(1, n+1):
        edges[u].sort()
    start = [0]*(n+1)
    end = [0]*(n+1)
    is_leaf = [False]*(n+1)
    leaves = []
    time = 0
    stack = [(1, False)]
    while stack:
        u, visited = stack.pop()
        if visited:
            end[u] = time
            continue
        start[u] = time
        time +=1
        stack.append((u, True))
        for v in reversed(edges[u]):
            stack.append((v, False))
    for u in range(1, n+1):
        if len(edges[u]) ==0 or (u ==1 and len(edges[u]) ==1):
            is_leaf[u] = True
            leaves.append(u)
        elif u !=1 and len(edges[u]) ==0:
            is_leaf[u] = True
            leaves.append(u)
    leaves.sort()
    m = len(leaves)
    leaf_pos = {v:i for i, v in enumerate(leaves)}
    leaf_depth = [0]*m
    for i in range(m):
        leaf_depth[i] = depth[leaves[i]]
    size = 1
    while size < m:
        size <<=1
    INF = 1 << 60
    seg = [INF]*(2*size)
    for i in range(m):
        seg[size +i] = leaf_depth[i]
    for i in range(size-1,0,-1):
        seg[i] = min(seg[2*i], seg[2*i+1])
    def query_seg(l, r):
        res = INF
        l += size
        r += size
        while l < r:
            if l%2:
                res = min(res, seg[l])
                l +=1
            if r%2:
                r -=1
                res = min(res, seg[r])
            l >>=1
            r >>=1
        return res
    ancestors = []
    for u in range(1, n+1):
        anc = []
        current = u
        while current !=0:
            anc.append(current)
            current = parent[current]
        ancestors.append(anc)
    for _ in range(q):
        v = int(data[idx])
        l = int(data[idx+1])
        r = int(data[idx+2])
        idx +=3
        min_dist = INF
        left = 0
        right = m
        while left < right:
            mid = (left + right) //2
            if leaves[mid] >= l:
                right = mid
            else:
                left = mid +1
        L = left
        left =0
        right = m
        while left < right:
            mid = (left + right)//2
            if leaves[mid] > r:
                right = mid
            else:
                left = mid +1
        R = left
        if L < R:
            current_min = query_seg(L, R)
            min_sub = current_min - depth[v]
            min_dist = min(min_dist, min_sub)
        s_v = start[v]
        e_v = end[v]
        for u in ancestors[v-1]:
            if u ==0:
                continue
            s_u = start[u]
            e_u = end[u]
            a = s_u
            b = s_v -1
            new_l = max(a, l)
            new_r = min(b, r)
            if new_l <= new_r:
                left = 0
                right = m
                while left < right:
                    mid = (left + right) //2
                    if leaves[mid] >= new_l:
                        right = mid
                    else:
                        left = mid +1
                L1 = left
                left =0
                right = m
                while left < right:
                    mid = (left + right)//2
                    if leaves[mid] > new_r:
                        right = mid
                    else:
                        left = mid +1
                R1 = left
                if L1 < R1:
                    current_min = query_seg(L1, R1)
                    current_val = current_min - 2 * depth[u]
                    min_dist = min(min_dist, current_val + depth[v])
            a = e_v +1
            b = e_u
            new_l = max(a, l)
            new_r = min(b, r)
            if new_l <= new_r:
                left =0

import sys
from collections import defaultdict, deque

sys.setrecursionlimit(1 << 25)

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read().split()
    idx = 0
    n, m = int(input[idx]), int(input[idx+1])
    idx +=2
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n+1)]
    for _ in range(m):
        u = int(input[idx])
        v = int(input[idx+1])
        adj[u].append(v)
        adj[v].append(u)
        idx +=2

    # Biconnected components decomposition using Tarjan's algorithm
    visited = [False]*(n+1)
    parent = [0]*(n+1)
    disc = [0]*(n+1)
    low = [0]*(n+1)
    time = 0
    stack = []
    bcc = []
    is_articulation = [False]*(n+1)

    def dfs(u):
        nonlocal time
        children =0
        disc[u] = low[u] = time
        time +=1
        visited[u] = True
        for v in adj[u]:
            if not visited[v]:
                parent[v] = u
                children +=1
                stack.append((u, v))
                dfs(v)
                low[u] = min(low[u], low[v])
                if (parent[u] ==0 and children >1) or (parent[u] !=0 and low[v] >= disc[u]):
                    is_articulation[u] = True
                    comp = []
                    while True:
                        edge = stack.pop()
                        comp.append(edge)
                        if edge == (u, v):
                            break
                    bcc.append(comp)
            elif v != parent[u] and disc[v] < disc[u]:
                stack.append((u, v))
                low[u] = min(low[u], disc[v])
        return

    for u in range(1, n+1):
        if not visited[u]:
            dfs(u)
            if stack:
                comp = []
                while stack:
                    comp.append(stack.pop())
                if comp:
                    bcc.append(comp)

    # Identify cycles and bridges
    cycle_nodes = defaultdict(list)
    node_cycle = {}
    bridge_edges = set()

    for component in bcc:
        edges = component
        nodes = set()
        for u, v in edges:
            nodes.add(u)
            nodes.add(v)
        edge_count = len(edges)
        if edge_count == len(nodes):
            bridge_edges.update((u, v) for u, v in edges)
            bridge_edges.update((v, u) for u, v in edges)
        else:
            # Assume it's a cycle
            cycle_id = len(cycle_nodes) +1
            for node in nodes:
                cycle_nodes[cycle_id].append(node)
                node_cycle[node] = cycle_id

    # For each node not in any cycle, mark as bridge node
    bridge_nodes = set()
    for node in range(1, n+1):
        if node not in node_cycle:
            bridge_nodes.add(node)

    # Find articulation points
    articulation_points = set()
    for node in range(1, n+1):
        if is_articulation[node]:
            articulation_points.add(node)

    # Compute max_depth for articulation points (placeholder)
    # This is a dummy approach and may not be correct
    max_depth = [0]*(n+1)

    # For each node in a cycle, compute answer
    ans = [0]*(n+1)
    for cycle_id in cycle_nodes:
        nodes_in_cycle = cycle_nodes[cycle_id]
        k = len(nodes_in_cycle)
        cycle_radius = (k-1 +1)//2  # ceil((k-1)/2)
        art_points = [node for node in nodes_in_cycle if node in articulation_points]
        for u in nodes_in_cycle:
            current_max = cycle_radius
            for v in art_points:
                # Minimal distance between u and v in the cycle
                # Since the cycle is undirected, minimal distance is min(d, k-d)
                # Dummy calculation (incorrect, need actual cycle order)
                d = 1  # placeholder
                current = d + max_depth[v]
                if current > current_max:
                    current_max = current
            ans[u] = current_max

    # For bridge nodes, compute max distance to leaf (placeholder)
    # This is a dummy BFS
    if bridge_nodes:
        # Build the tree without cycles
        tree = [[] for _ in range(n+1)]
        for u, v in bridge_edges:
            tree[u].append(v)
        # Compute max distance for each node
        def bfs(start):
            visited = [False]*(n+1)
            q = deque()
            q.append((start, 0))
            visited[start] = True
            max_dist = 0
            while q:
                u, d = q.popleft()
                max_dist = d
                for v in tree[u]:
                    if not visited[v]:
                        visited[v] = True
                        q.append((v, d+1))
            return max_dist
        for u in bridge_nodes:
            ans[u] = bfs(u)

    print(' '.join(map(str, ans[1:n+1])))
